paragraphs: Agent0-VL addresses a weakness in models that judge their own visual reasoning: a text-only critique can itself contain unsupported claims about an image. The proposed agent uses tools during reasoning, evaluation, and repair, so that its attempts to improve can draw on visual evidence rather than relying entirely on its own written explanations.

A single vision-language model takes on two roles. The Solver works through problems using multiple rounds of tool-assisted reasoning. The Verifier uses tools to produce structured criticism and detailed rewards for that reasoning. A repeated learning cycle combines these checks with reinforcement learning, bringing the model’s reasoning behavior and evaluation behavior into closer alignment as they evolve together.

The reported evolution process uses neither human annotations nor an external reward model. Experiments cover chart reasoning, geometry problems, and visual scientific analysis, with a reported 12.5% improvement over the Qwen-VL base model. These results support tool-grounded self-evaluation as a route to improvement within the studied tasks, extending tool use from answering questions to assessing and repairing the reasoning behind answers.
icml-2026-agent0-vl-exploring-self-evolv.tldr: Agent0-VL improves visual reasoning by using tools to ground its own solving, verification, and repair cycle without external rewards.

paragraphs: AnalogVerifier automates the creation of testbenches for analog circuits, where checking a design requires interpreting varied specifications and translating them into precise tests. The paper identifies a mismatch between language models’ probabilistic text generation and verification’s need for deterministic ordering, numerical accuracy, and satisfaction of circuit constraints.

The framework separates interpreting specifications from enforcing their logical consequences. An agentic workflow breaks specifications into individual tasks. Port Dependency Graphs then organize those tasks into sequences that satisfy analog design constraints by construction. Numerical thresholds come from a deterministic symbolic component, reducing reliance on a language model to derive exact values. Simulation feedback closes the loop by guiding repairs to generated testbenches.

Across five industrial analog circuits, the system achieves functional pass rates ranging from 82.3% to 100%. Those results demonstrate substantial success on the evaluated designs while preserving the distinction between high pass rates and universal correctness. The central contribution is a division of responsibilities: language-based processing handles specification meaning, while graph structure, symbolic calculations, and simulation provide more constrained checks on the resulting tests.
icml-2026-analogverifier-a-neuro-symboli.tldr: AnalogVerifier combines language-model interpretation, symbolic enforcement, and simulation feedback to automate analog-circuit testbench generation.

paragraphs: AFS targets visual hallucinations: generated words that do not match the image evidence. It builds a training signal from differences between predictions made at intermediate model layers and those made at the final layer. This gives the model an internal basis for focusing its optimization on potentially unreliable visual descriptions.

The framework selectively supervises visually descriptive tokens, incorporates token classification that accounts for hallucination, and encourages agreement between intermediate and final prediction distributions. It uses Group Relative Policy Optimization with rewards specific to individual tokens. These rewards come from internal model signals, making the approach an optimization method rather than a correction applied only after an answer has been generated.

The experiments report significantly fewer hallucinations in image captions without reducing recall. That combination matters because fewer unsupported descriptions need not come at the cost of overlooking supported content. The paper also reports improved object-existence judgments and multimodal reasoning, together with transfer across visual datasets. The findings suggest that the internal signals used by AFS can support reliability beyond the caption-generation setting.
icml-2026-anchor-final-self-supervision-.tldr: AFS uses disagreements between model layers to create token-level training rewards that reduce visual hallucinations while preserving caption recall.

paragraphs: PACE addresses factuality control when the questions reaching a language model change over time. Existing conformal approaches rely on exchangeability, an assumption that often breaks in online use as users’ interests shift. The resulting challenge is to keep the observed error behavior close to a target while the incoming data changes.

The framework repeatedly updates a time-varying target miscoverage parameter using an adaptive step size. It combines a proactive signal estimating distribution shifts with a reactive signal measuring the local coverage gap. The first responds to evidence that the data has changed; the second responds to errors already observed. The design is motivated by theoretical relationships between expected miscoverage, distribution shifts, and parameter error.

Experiments on synthetic and real-world data report improvements over advanced adaptive alternatives. In question answering, deviation from the target error rate falls by up to 60%, and coverage recovery after abrupt shifts accelerates by more than 2.5 times. These are findings about maintaining aggregate coverage behavior under change, rather than a claim that every individual answer becomes factual.
icml-2026-beyond-reactivity-proactive-ad.tldr: PACE combines shift detection with observed coverage errors to adapt factuality control as online language-model queries change.

paragraphs: DiNa-LRM learns preference rewards directly from the noisy internal states of a diffusion model. The paper motivates this choice with two issues in using vision-language models as reward providers: their computational expense and the mismatch between a generator working in latent space and a reward evaluated on pixels.

The method reuses a pretrained latent diffusion backbone and adds a reward head conditioned on the diffusion timestep. Its preference likelihood explicitly accounts for uncertainty that changes with diffusion noise. This lets the reward model treat different noise levels as part of the scoring problem. At inference time, noise ensembling combines reward evidence across noisy evaluations, providing a way to spend additional computation on more robust scoring.

On image alignment benchmarks, the approach substantially outperforms existing diffusion-based reward methods and performs competitively with leading vision-language models at substantially lower computational cost. The paper also reports faster, more resource-efficient preference optimization. Together, these findings support matching the reward model’s representation to the generator’s own diffusion process as a useful route to efficient alignment.
icml-2026-beyond-vlm-based-rewards-diffu.tldr: DiNa-LRM scores preferences within noisy diffusion latents, offering competitive image rewards and more efficient model alignment.

paragraphs: CalMRL tackles multimodal learning when some examples lack one or more modalities. Methods that align every modality around a shared representation can struggle with such incomplete examples. The paper explains this through anchor shift: the alignment reference formed from available modalities differs from the reference that would be obtained if all modalities were present.

The proposed method calibrates these incomplete alignments by using prior information and relationships among modalities to model missing representations. Its imputation takes place in representation space, where alignment occurs. To handle the resulting optimization problem, CalMRL uses a two-step learning procedure that incorporates a closed-form posterior distribution for shared latent variables.

The paper provides theoretical guidance on convergence and mitigation of anchor shift, and reports experimental superiority. Combining calibrated alignment with an existing advanced method allows that method to absorb examples with missing modalities, which it could not originally accommodate. The contribution therefore concerns both representation quality and the range of usable training data: incomplete observations can participate in multimodal alignment through an explicit correction for their shifted reference.
icml-2026-calibrated-multimodal-represen.tldr: CalMRL corrects alignment shifts caused by missing modalities by modeling missing information directly in representation space.

paragraphs: Cardio-mmFlow addresses a data shortage in contactless cardiac sensing. Reconstructing ECG from millimeter-wave radar is constrained by limited high-quality synchronized recordings. The paper approaches that shortage by synthesizing radar signals from clinical ECG, creating data intended to help the downstream task of recovering ECG from radar measurements.

The model learns a direct flow between ECG and radar latent representations without a Gaussian prior. To account for differences in signal propagation between people, it incorporates a simplified modulation inspired by a mass–spring–damper system. This information changes the flow dynamics through feature-wise linear modulation, giving the synthesis process a mechanism for personalization rather than treating every subject’s propagation characteristics identically.

Experiments report high fidelity in both generated signals and their latent representations. The synthetic data significantly improves the downstream zero-shot radar-to-ECG task and enables atrial fibrillation classification using synthetic data. Additional analyses examine interpretability. These findings support the proposed synthesis method as a way to strengthen data-constrained sensing models; the reported contribution centers on generated data and downstream modeling performance.
icml-2026-cardio-mmflow-a-gaussian-prior.tldr: Cardio-mmFlow synthesizes personalized radar signals from ECG to improve data-constrained contactless cardiac modeling.

paragraphs: CDAL addresses two obstacles in fair clustering from multiple views of the same data: preserving useful cluster structure while limiting sensitive information, and avoiding computational costs that grow quadratically with dataset size. Its approach makes the separation of semantic and sensitive information part of the representation’s structure.

Guided by a structural causal model perspective, the method uses two sets of anchors to organize latent representations into orthogonal semantic and sensitive subspaces. It also applies a linearized Hilbert–Schmidt Independence Criterion constraint to enforce statistical independence. These mechanisms address different aspects of separation: the subspaces provide structural organization, while the independence constraint addresses statistical relationships between the factors. An alternating optimization scheme makes the training procedure efficient.

The paper proves identifiability of the disentangled factors and global convergence for its algorithm, with time complexity linear in the number of examples. Experiments on large datasets report a better utility–fairness trade-off than existing leading methods. The findings combine a theoretical account of the learned separation with empirical evidence that fairness and useful clustering can be balanced more effectively at scale.
icml-2026-causal-disentangled-anchor-lea.tldr: CDAL separates semantic and sensitive information to improve the fairness–utility trade-off in clustering with linear-time scaling.

paragraphs: This paper gives value clipping in Q-learning a robustness interpretation. The algorithm limits the value estimate used in a Bellman update by a threshold. The theoretical result is that this clipped update provides an unbiased single-sample estimate of a robust Bellman operator arising from a transition-regularized decision-process formulation.

The corresponding robustness concerns a particular class of adversarial changes to environment dynamics: transition probability is moved away from high-value states. Under this interpretation, clipped Q-learning learns against that adverse possibility, producing more conservative decisions. The claim is specific to this perturbation class, rather than a guarantee against every possible environmental change. The authors also analyze two variants with optimistic exploration bonuses and establish polynomial regret guarantees.

Beyond tabular problems, the framework suggests that clipping could serve as a modular addition to value-based algorithms using function approximation. A clipped Double DQN experiment on one control task provides a proof of concept, showing robustness improvements consistent with the theory. The contribution connects a simple numerical operation to a precise objective for hedging against adverse dynamics.
icml-2026-clipped-q-learning-your-value-.tldr: Clipped Q-learning has a theoretical interpretation as learning robustly against specific adverse changes in transition probabilities.

paragraphs: CoME organizes a mobile agent around four capabilities: summarizing the screen, planning subtasks, deciding actions, and producing action functions. The motivation is that these stages need both specialized improvement and coordinated execution. The architecture assigns each stage its own expert and activates the corresponding expert when generating that stage’s output tokens.

Training proceeds through three phases. Expert-FT develops the individual capabilities separately. Router-FT teaches the system to activate the expert appropriate to each reasoning stage. CoT-FT then trains collaboration across the stages and balances their optimization. This progression gives specialization and integration distinct roles in training, while retaining a single reasoning process that combines their outputs.

The paper also introduces InfoGain-Driven DPO to reduce the spread of errors through intermediate reasoning. It evaluates each step’s contribution using information gain and favors more informative reasoning. Experiments on AITZ and AMEX show improvements over dense mobile agents and mixture-of-experts methods. The results support pairing stage-specific experts with training that explicitly manages both their coordination and the usefulness of intermediate steps.
icml-2026-come-empowering-channel-of-mob.tldr: CoME trains four stage-specific mobile-agent experts and uses information gain to improve their coordinated reasoning.

paragraphs: STPDE tackles forecasting across space and time when environmental conditions change. The paper argues that separating shared dynamics from local environmental variation is difficult for existing approaches based largely on discrete graph inference. It instead represents the evolving system through inhomogeneous partial differential equations, making spatially varying conditions an explicit part of the formulation.

The framework splits dynamics into an invariant diffusion operator for shared mechanisms and an environment basis manifold for local differences. This separates how information spreads from the medium-specific conditions affecting that spread. The authors show that linear attention can effectively approximate the Laplacian’s Green’s function, enabling global diffusion at scale. Stochastic environmental perturbations complement this representation to improve robustness under changing conditions.

Experiments cover ordinary forecasting, generalization beyond the training distribution, transfer between cities with few examples, and continual learning. The paper reports consistent improvements over leading baselines with competitive computational efficiency. Across these settings, the findings support explicitly modeling stable mechanisms and environmental variation as separate components, rather than expecting a single undifferentiated representation to handle both.
icml-2026-decoupling-universal-laws-and-.tldr: STPDE separates shared spatial dynamics from local environmental variation to improve forecasting under distribution shifts.

paragraphs: DMSampler reduces the cost of generating samples during online reinforcement learning for diffusion models. Repeated policy rollouts typically require roughly 50 denoising steps in the setting described. The framework uses a distilled proxy that produces reward-evaluation samples in 4–8 steps, reducing rollout cost by an order of magnitude.

Training alternates between improving the policy and refreshing the proxy. During reinforcement learning, hybrid sampling combines samples from the old policy with those from the distilled sampler. During distillation, the sampler is brought back into alignment with the updated policy. Hybrid sampling preserves on-policy structure, while reward-aware distillation reuses high-reward trajectories to reduce the loss of useful behavior during compression.

Experiments in text-to-image and text-to-video generation report improvements on OCR, GenEval, and VBench alongside substantially fewer GPU hours. The method also works with multiple diffusion reinforcement-learning optimizers. The key finding is that a continually refreshed small-step sampler can support policy improvement efficiently: its speed is useful because training also maintains its connection to the changing policy and its successful trajectories.
icml-2026-distillation-models-are-good-s.tldr: DMSampler accelerates diffusion reinforcement learning with a few-step sampling proxy that is repeatedly distilled from the improving policy.

paragraphs: Dr. Kernel studies how to train language models to generate efficient Triton kernels. The paper highlights two failures in reinforcement learning for this task: exploiting the reward mechanism and settling for correct code without meaningful speed improvements. Its contribution combines a training environment, changes to learning signals, and profiling-based optimization.

KernelGYM provides distributed GPU execution, reward-hacking checks, collection of multi-turn interactions, and support for sustained training. The authors identify bias from self-inclusion in GRPO’s policy-gradient calculation and introduce Turn-level Reinforce-Leave-One-Out for unbiased advantage estimation. They also apply mismatch correction for stability and use profiling-based rewards and rejection sampling to encourage actual optimization rather than correctness alone.

The resulting Dr. Kernel-14B model achieves performance competitive with Claude-4.5-Sonnet on Kernelbench. With sequential test-time scaling, it surpasses GPT-5 and Claude-4.5-Sonnet on the benchmark’s level-2 subset. The latter result is tied to that subset and additional sequential computation. Overall, the findings connect kernel-generation performance to the quality of the execution environment, feedback, and multi-turn reinforcement-learning procedure.
icml-2026-dr-kernel-reinforcement-learni.tldr: Dr. Kernel combines robust GPU evaluation, corrected multi-turn learning, and profiling feedback to train models that generate faster Triton kernels.

paragraphs: PWC-Diff aims to recognize properties of radio signals despite the changes they undergo while traveling through a wireless channel. Received signals can be distorted by effects such as fading. The paper argues that learning directly from those distorted observations, or using diffusion only for denoising, leaves important channel effects insufficiently addressed.

The framework incorporates physical wireless-channel priors into the diffusion process. It progressively learns to remove channel effects and recover a representation closer to the transmitted signal. Its FusedFormer architecture combines fusion and self-attention modules to capture both temporal and spectral characteristics throughout the diffusion trajectory. This makes the physical transmission process part of representation recovery, rather than treating all corruption as generic noise.

Experiments across several datasets and three wireless signal recognition tasks report state-of-the-art performance. Ablation studies further support the effectiveness of the proposed framework. These findings provide empirical backing for including channel knowledge in diffusion-based signal understanding. The stated target is a representation closer to the transmitted signal, which connects physical recovery to recognition without claiming exact reconstruction of every transmitted waveform.
icml-2026-from-denoising-to-de-channelin.tldr: PWC-Diff integrates wireless-channel knowledge into diffusion to recover more useful radio-signal representations for recognition.

paragraphs: This paper examines why audio-visual deepfake detection becomes harder when videos shift from talking to singing. Existing detectors often depend on inconsistencies between sound and visible movement. Rhythmic vocalization weakens that relationship, creating a domain shift that substantially reduces detection performance. The authors introduce Singing Head DeepFake, a dataset built with rhythm-aware generative models, to study this setting.

Their T-AVFD framework combines facial authenticity patterns with audio-visual consistency. A pattern learner aligns facial features with textual descriptions at multiple levels of detail, aiming to learn authenticity cues that transfer across scenarios. A second module adaptively weights those cues alongside the intrinsic relationship between audio and video, rather than assigning the same importance to each source of evidence.

Experiments on multiple talking-head datasets and the new singing dataset show consistent improvements over existing baselines and robustness under diverse perturbations. The contribution is both an evaluation setting and a detection strategy. It demonstrates the value of supplementing cross-modal consistency with facial authenticity evidence when the relationship between voice and movement changes across kinds of performance.
icml-2026-from-talking-to-singing-a-new-.tldr: A new singing-deepfake dataset and text-guided detector address the shift in audio-visual cues between speech and song.

paragraphs: M-IDoL addresses a representation problem in medical foundation models trained across imaging modalities. Combining all images in one embedding space can blur the information that distinguishes modalities and the detail within each modality. The paper seeks representations that preserve both kinds of structure while remaining useful across downstream clinical tasks.

Its self-supervised training has two complementary objectives. The first maximizes inter-modality entropy by distributing representations across separable mixture-of-experts subspaces, promoting modality specificity. The second minimizes uncertainty within each modality through fine-grained semantic discrimination inside those subspaces. Together, these objectives aim to distinguish imaging types while also retaining meaningful variation among images of the same type.

After pretraining on 1.15 million medical images, M-IDoL outperforms 20 foundation models across 21 downstream clinical tasks spanning five modalities: X-ray, fundus, OCT, dermoscopy, and pathology. Representation analyses show clearer separation between modalities and finer discrimination within them. These findings connect the method’s explicit decomposition objectives with both the organization of learned features and stronger generalization on the evaluated tasks.
icml-2026-m-idol-information-decompositi.tldr: M-IDoL separates medical imaging modalities into expert subspaces while preserving fine-grained information within each modality.

paragraphs: MathlibLemma focuses on reusable intermediate facts that mathematicians often assume but formal libraries may lack. These missing folklore lemmas can make Lean less convenient for everyday mathematical work, even when the broader formal-reasoning ecosystem is strong. The paper uses language models to discover, formalize, and prove such facts proactively.

The modular pipeline produces a library containing 1,506 Lean-checked proofs that also pass a proof-bypass screen. A small curated pilot subset has been merged into Mathlib. That external acceptance supports the quality of those selected outputs against expert library standards, while remaining a narrower result than acceptance of the entire generated collection.

The authors also build a benchmark of 4,028 non-trivial, type-checked Lean statements across multiple mathematical domains. The benchmark statements and the verified proof library are distinct outputs: type checking a statement and supplying its proof serve different purposes. Together, the outputs support a shift toward models that contribute missing mathematical infrastructure, adding reusable connective facts rather than only solving problems against a fixed existing library.
icml-2026-mathliblemma-folklore-lemma-ge.tldr: MathlibLemma mines missing reusable mathematical facts, producing checked Lean proofs and a benchmark of formal statements.

paragraphs: OptiVer addresses the difficulty of checking mathematical optimization models generated by language models. Translating a problem description into variables and constraints requires substantial expertise. A generated formulation can fail to capture the original requirements, and its solutions can expose additional problems. Weak verification makes subsequent correction less effective.

The framework checks the formulation from two perspectives. Structure-side verification examines whether the variables, constraints, and overall model reflect the original problem description. Solution-side verification interprets the model’s solutions and evaluates their validity. The two views connect what the formulation says with what it actually permits as an answer, giving the correction process evidence about both representation and consequences.

Experiments on several popular benchmarks report an accuracy improvement of over 20% compared with the state of the art. The abstract does not specify that this is a percentage-point increase, so the result is best retained in its reported form. The main methodological finding is that checking both model structure and solution validity improves automated optimization modeling beyond relying on an unchecked generated formulation.
icml-2026-opt-verifier-unleashing-the-po.tldr: OptiVer improves language-model-generated optimization formulations by checking both their structure and the validity of their solutions.

paragraphs: Ramba is a selective state-space model designed to learn directly from databases containing multiple related tables. The paper targets a tension between large-context access and efficiency: Transformer costs grow quadratically, while graph neural networks give up global context to remain efficient. Ramba aims to process broad relational context while retaining relevant information selectively.

Topology-Aware Linearization arranges cells into a global column-based sequence with linear processing complexity. Sparse attention masks for entities and foreign keys recover relational structure within that sequence. Schema Dynamic Gating then adjusts state transitions according to the semantic relationship between the attribute currently being read and the prediction target. This filters relevance across tables using schema meaning rather than relying on value distributions.

Experiments across relational benchmarks report state-of-the-art performance with linear scalability. The architectural contribution joins an efficient sequential representation with mechanisms that preserve database relationships and prediction-specific relevance. The findings suggest that large relational contexts can be useful without requiring every cell to interact densely with every other cell during processing.
icml-2026-ramba-selective-state-space-mo.tldr: Ramba combines selective state-space processing with relational structure and schema-aware gating to learn efficiently across database tables.

paragraphs: This paper changes the representation used during diffusion-based 3D shape generation. Dense grids, meshes, and point clouds can require thousands to millions of values, making each denoising step expensive. The proposed method instead represents a shape with a small collection of superquadrics, geometric primitives described by pose, size, and shape parameters.

The diffusion state uses 7KB of superquadric parameters, sharply reducing its dimensionality and per-step computation and memory requirements. Generated primitives can then be decoded into point clouds without fixing the diffusion representation to a particular output resolution. The same compact structure supports part-level editing and constraint-based design, connecting computational savings with more direct control over geometric components.

On standard benchmarks, the decoded point clouds achieve competitive surface fidelity and distributional performance. Generation takes at most 0.6 seconds per shape under most conditions reported in the abstract. The result shows that compact geometric structure can support efficient generation and useful editing capabilities while maintaining competitive evaluated quality; the speed claim remains qualified by the stated range of conditions.
icml-2026-rethinking-3d-shape-generation.tldr: Generating compact superquadric parameters makes 3D diffusion cheaper while supporting part editing and competitive decoded shape quality.

paragraphs: SSLogic expands reasoning-training data by evolving task families rather than repeatedly varying examples from fixed templates. The paper identifies fixed synthesis rules as a bottleneck for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. Its agents create executable generator–validator pairs, allowing the synthesis process to introduce new rules and ranges of difficulty.

A repeated generate, validate, and refine loop develops these task families. Multiple validation gates combine different solving strategies with adversarial blind review, where independent agents write and execute code to solve instances. These checks filter ill-posed tasks before training. Starting from 400 seed families, two evolution rounds produce 953 families and 21,389 verifiable instances.

Comparisons matched by training steps, tokens, and external-data size consistently find greater training utility for the evolved data. The reported Enigmata comparisons include gains of 5.2 on SynLogic, 3.0 on AIME25, and 5.5 on BBH. KORBench shows selective gains in logic and operation categories. The findings support structural diversity in task generation as a useful source of downstream reasoning improvement, beyond merely increasing variations of existing problems.
icml-2026-scaling-the-scaling-logic-agen.tldr: SSLogic uses agents to evolve and validate new logic-task families, producing training data with stronger reported reasoning utility.

paragraphs: SHINE turns supplied context into a LoRA adapter in a single forward pass. The aim is to make context-specific knowledge available through model parameters, so the language model can answer related complex questions without directly accessing the original context. This changes how adaptation is performed after the hypernetwork has been trained.

The hypernetwork reuses the frozen language model’s own parameters and adds architectural changes to obtain strong expressive capacity with relatively few parameters. It is trained through pretraining and instruction fine-tuning to map diverse meaningful contexts into adapters. For a new context, generating the adapter does not require a separate fine-tuning process, although learning the adapter-generation mechanism itself does require training.

The paper reports strong results across several tasks and substantial savings in time, computation, and memory compared with adaptation based on supervised fine-tuning. It also reports promising scaling potential. The contribution is the learned conversion from context to a parameter update: one trained mechanism produces context-specific adaptations directly, making repeated adaptation less dependent on running an optimization procedure for each new context.
icml-2026-shine-a-scalable-in-context-hy.tldr: SHINE generates context-specific LoRA adapters in one pass, enabling related question answering without per-context fine-tuning.

paragraphs: SRLS automates the choice of features and steering strength for training-free image editing with diffusion models. The task requires changing a target attribute while preserving unrelated content and visual quality. Sparse autoencoder features offer interpretable controls, but selecting them heuristically and adjusting their strength manually can produce poor trade-offs among these objectives.

The method formulates steering-vector discovery as a convex sparse recovery problem using the affine structure of the autoencoder decoder. A Lasso objective selects a small support set of features. Ridge refitting restricted to that selected set then debiases the coefficients. This separates deciding which features to use from refining how strongly those chosen features should contribute to the steering vector.

A fixed-budget Bayesian optimization procedure replaces manual strength tuning. Across varied subjects and attributes, the paper reports a better balance of target alignment, preservation of non-target content, and image quality than competing methods. The findings support using a structured optimization procedure for interpretable feature control, with both feature selection and strength adjustment treated as explicit parts of the editing problem.
icml-2026-sparse-relaxed-lasso-steering-.tldr: SRLS automatically selects sparse autoencoder features and tunes their strength to improve precise, training-free image editing.

paragraphs: TimeRewarder learns signals of task progress from passive videos so that reinforcement learning can receive feedback at individual steps. Such dense rewards are useful in robotics but often require substantial manual design. The paper uses the progression visible in robot demonstrations and human videos as a source of supervision for estimating progress.

The method models temporal distances between pairs of frames and converts progress estimates into step-wise proxy rewards. These rewards guide learning on tasks whose original rewards are sparse. Their role is to supply more frequent information about advancement toward completion, using a learned visual measure rather than requiring a manually specified dense reward for each task.

On ten Meta-World tasks, TimeRewarder achieves nearly perfect success on nine with 200,000 environment interactions per task. It outperforms previous methods and the manually designed environment dense reward in final success and sample efficiency. The paper also demonstrates pretraining with real-world human videos. Together, these findings support passive video as a potentially scalable source of reward information, with the strongest quantitative evidence coming from the reported Meta-World experiments.
icml-2026-timerewarder-learning-dense-re.tldr: TimeRewarder turns temporal relationships in passive videos into dense proxy rewards that improve robotic reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: VideoTemp-o3 addresses long-video questions whose answers depend on evidence that uniform frame sampling may miss. Agentic approaches try to locate a relevant segment, inspect it densely, and then answer. The paper identifies weak localization, inefficient processing, and rigid workflows as remaining obstacles in that approach.

The proposed framework jointly models temporal grounding and question answering. It can request clips when needed and revise inaccurate localizations, allowing evidence selection to interact with understanding. During supervised fine-tuning, a unified masking mechanism encourages exploration while limiting noise. Reinforcement learning adds dedicated rewards intended to reduce reward hacking, supporting the joint training of useful localization and answering behavior.

The authors also develop a pipeline for constructing high-quality grounded question-answer data for long videos and a benchmark covering different video durations. Experiments report strong performance in both long-video understanding and grounding. The combined contribution treats locating evidence as an adaptable part of reasoning, supported by training data and evaluation that address both where relevant events occur and what those events mean for an answer.
icml-2026-videotemp-o3-harmonizing-tempo.tldr: VideoTemp-o3 jointly learns video localization and question answering, allowing an agent to request clips and refine its evidence selection.
